changed.title: The 4 by 4 bipartite graph with mask 4396 is represented on the one-a-side promise by an AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in two with at most 6 gates
changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ C.size ≤ 6 ∧ PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun u v : Fin 4 => (4396 : ℕ).testBit (4 * u.val + v.val)) C
changed.unlocks: A witness prices the gate saving from negation on mask 4396. Compare its shared and negated wires with the checked AND/OR minimum for the same graph.
changed.sketch: Encode the 16 promised input pairs as wire truth tables. Start with the 4 row masks and 4 column masks. For each of at most 6 gates choose earlier wires and AND, OR or NOT. Order binary operands to remove duplicates. Match every output bit to mask 4396. Among circuits of this size at least one NOT is needed by the checked AND/OR floor. Return a gate list and replay all 16 output bits.

changed.title: Positive accumulation points of 2-CNF densities are exactly half the attainable positive densities
changed.statement:
let W := fun width : ℕ => Fin width → Bool
let F := fun arity : ℕ => Finset ((Fin arity × Bool) × (Fin arity × Bool))
let sat := fun (len : ℕ) (A : F len) (x : W len) => decide (∀ c ∈ A,
  x c.1.1 ≠ c.1.2 ∨ x c.2.1 ≠ c.2.2)
let den := fun (size : ℕ) (G : F size) =>
  ((Finset.univ.filter (fun w : W size => sat size G w = true)).card : ℝ) / 2 ^ size
∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → t ≤ 1 →
  (∃ gap : ℝ, 0 < gap ∧ ∀ (n : ℕ) (A : F n), den n A < t → den n A ≤ t - gap) ∧
  ((∀ e : ℝ, 0 < e → ∃ (n : ℕ) (A : F n), t < den n A ∧ den n A < t + e) ↔
    ∃ (d : ℕ) (B : F d), den d B = 2 * t) ∧
  (∃ K : ℕ, ∀ (n : ℕ) (A : F n), t ≤ den n A →
    ∃ (S : Finset (Fin n)) (B : F n),
      S.card ≤ K ∧ (∀ c ∈ B, c.1.1 ∈ S ∧ c.2.1 ∈ S) ∧
      t ≤ den n B ∧ ∀ z : W n, sat n B z = true → sat n A z = true)
changed.unlocks: Classifies the positive thresholds where hidden binary formulas can approach the cutoff from above.
changed.context: At density bounded away from zero a maximal disjoint clause packing gives a bounded vertex cover. Group other bits by their signed clauses into that cover. Along a subsequence each type multiplicity is fixed or tends to infinity. Given cover bits a growing type is free, forced or impossible. Only free types survive in the limit. Making them all free pins cover literals, yielding a bounded stronger formula of the limiting density. A nonempty growing type pins at least one bit. Remove one pin to double the limit. Conversely multiply by larger signed stars.

Conversely multiply by larger signed stars.

changed.title: One row exposure order and decoder thin the optimal paired OR loss at every size of a finite square table
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (F : Fin n → Fin n → Bool),
  ∃ order : Equiv.Perm (Fin n),
    let exposed := fun h : ℕ => Finset.univ.filter (fun i : Fin n => h ≤ (order i).val)
    let cost := fun (h : ℕ) (out : Finset (Fin n) → Finset (Fin n) → Bool) =>
      (Finset.univ.filter (fun z : Fin n × Fin n =>
        out ({z.1,z.2} : Finset (Fin n)) (exposed h ∩ {z.1}) ≠ F z.1 z.2)).card
    ∃ D : Finset (Fin n) → Finset (Fin n) → Bool,
      (∀ h : ℕ, h ≤ n → ∀ other, cost h D ≤ cost h other) ∧
      (∀ h : ℕ, 1 < h → h ≤ n → h * cost (h-1) D ≤ (h-2) * cost h D) ∧
      (∀ h : ℕ, h ≤ n → n*(n-1)*cost h D ≤ h*(h-1)*cost n D)
changed.unlocks: constructs one exposure order and one optimal unordered-pair decoder controlling errors at every hidden size
changed.context: Join two distinct labels when their table entries in opposite orientations differ. Expose a maximum-degree label in the current hidden graph. With h vertices and E edges its degree d satisfies hd ≥ 2E. Assign this vertex rank h-1. A decoder uses the reported row if present and otherwise takes the earlier endpoint as row. With one exposed endpoint it is exact, and on each discordant hidden edge it makes precisely one unavoidable error. Thus e_h=E, giving the step inequality. Telescope for h≥2 and treat zero or one hidden label directly.

changed.title: A central Hamming band has induced matchings with short binary syndromes and an exponentially small exceptional set
changed.statement:
∀ n : ℕ,
  let X := Fin n → Bool
  let wt := fun v : X => (Finset.univ.filter (fun j : Fin n => v j = true)).card
  let diff := fun (x y : X) (j : Fin n) => xor (x j) (y j)
  let central := fun d : ℕ => 16 * Nat.dist (2*d) n ≤ n
  let tails := Finset.univ.filter (fun v : X => ¬central (wt v))
  let f := 1+(3*n+7)/8
  let vec := fun (x : X) (j : Fin n) => if x j then (1 : ZMod 2) else 0
  tails.card * 2^(n/512) ≤ 2^(n+1) ∧
    ∃ H : (Fin n → ZMod 2) →ₗ[ZMod 2] (Fin f → ZMod 2),
      (∀ x y : X, x ≠ y → wt (diff x y) ≤ n/16 → H (vec x) ≠ H (vec y)) ∧
      ∀ p q : X × X, p ≠ q → central (wt (diff p.1 p.2)) → central (wt (diff q.1 q.2)) →
        (∀ j, (p.1 j).toNat + (p.2 j).toNat = (q.1 j).toNat + (q.2 j).toNat) →
        H (vec p.1) = H (vec q.1) →
        ¬central (wt (diff p.1 q.2)) ∧ ¬central (wt (diff q.1 p.2))
changed.unlocks: packs central pairs and bounds the number of tail masks for a systematic encoder with one check bit
changed.context: The two fair-binomial tails outside n/2 +/- n/32 have combined probability at most 2 exp(-n/512). The number of masks of weight at most n/16 is bounded by 16^(n/16)(17/16)^n <= 2^(3n/8). A random binary matrix of the stated height detects every nonzero such mask with positive probability. Equal coordinate sums force equal distances d. Distinct left endpoints of equal syndrome differ in more than n/16 positions. Each crossed distance is d minus that many positions, below the central band.

Equal coordinate sums force equal distances d. Distinct left endpoints of equal syndrome differ in more than n/16 positions. Each crossed distance is d minus that many positions, below the central band.

changed.title: Digit sums and a binary syndrome color every squared-distance bucket on a finite grid
changed.statement:
∀ (m b h : ℕ), 0 < b →
  let Q := 2^b
  let X := Fin m → Fin Q
  let width := m*Q^2 / 2^h + 1
  let distance := fun (x y : X) => ∑ j : Fin m, (Nat.dist (x j).val (y j).val)^2
  let bucket := fun (x y : X) => distance x y / width
  let f := 1+m+b*width
  let vec := fun (x : X) (i : Fin m × Fin b) => if (x i.1).val.testBit i.2.val then
    (1 : ZMod 2) else 0
  (∀ x y : X, bucket x y < 2^h) ∧
    ∃ H : ((Fin m × Fin b) → ZMod 2) →ₗ[ZMod 2] (Fin f → ZMod 2),
      (∀ x y : X, x ≠ y → (Finset.univ.filter (fun j : Fin m => x j ≠ y j)).card ≤ width →
        H (vec x) ≠ H (vec y)) ∧
      ∀ p q : X × X, p ≠ q → bucket p.1 p.2 = bucket q.1 q.2 →
        (∀ j, (p.1 j).val + (p.2 j).val = (q.1 j).val + (q.2 j).val) →
        H (vec p.1) = H (vec q.1) →
        bucket p.1 q.2 < bucket p.1 p.2 ∧ bucket q.1 p.2 < bucket p.1 p.2
changed.unlocks: prices the syndrome and proves agreement for a tag applied to every possible pair of raw payloads
changed.context: Every squared distance is below 2^h times the bucket width W. A difference supported on at most W digits is specified by its support mask and at most W b-bit values in position order. Some binary matrix with 1+m+bW rows detects them all by the union bound. Equal sums and distinct equal-syndrome left endpoints imply their squared distance exceeds W. Each crossed squared distance is the average of the two original distances minus that quantity. Both crosses fall strictly below the common bucket.

Some binary matrix with 1+m+bW rows detects them all by the union bound. Equal sums and distinct equal-syndrome left endpoints imply their squared distance exceeds W. Each crossed squared distance is the average of the two original distances minus that quantity. Both crosses fall strictly below the common bucket.

changed.title: Find a sparse matrix selector beating the bound that charges each NOT gate separately
changed.statement:
∃ (n m d : ℕ) (G : Fin n → Fin m → Bool) (edge : Bool)
    (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit),
  let nbrR := fun (a : Fin n) => Finset.univ.filter (fun v : Fin m => G a v = edge)
  let nbrC := fun (c : Fin m) => Finset.univ.filter (fun u : Fin n => G u c = edge)
  2 ≤ d ∧
  (∀ a, 2 ≤ (nbrR a).card ∧ (nbrR a).card ≤ d) ∧
  (∀ c, 2 ≤ (nbrC c).card ∧ (nbrC c).card ≤ d) ∧
  (∀ a b, a ≠ b → ((nbrR a) ∩ (nbrR b)).card ≤ 1) ∧
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ PEqualNP.Represents.Represents G C ∧
  let negs := C.gates.countP (fun g => @decide (g.op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.not) (Classical.propDecidable _))
  28 * d * C.size + 78 * d + 2 < (28 * d + 1) * (n + m) + 12 * d * negs
changed.unlocks: tests the weighted sparse lower bound on both polarities
changed.context: A union of bipartite cycles on 120 vertices admits d=2. With 119 gates even a circuit without a negation would violate the bound. A shared negation permits additional gates if it replaces enough repeated adjacency tests. Try both marked values and check every cross-component input pair. No violating witness is held.

A shared negation permits additional gates if it replaces enough repeated adjacency tests. Try both marked values and check every cross-component input pair. No violating witness is held.

changed.title: Minimally unsatisfiable hidden clauses characterize exact width and cost budgets for an OR of disjoint conjunctions
changed.statement:
∀ (n m hiddenCount W K : ℕ), 0 < n → 0 < m → ∀ price : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ lo hi, lo ≤ hi → price lo ≤ price hi) →
  let Raw := Fin m × Fin n
  let Cl := PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Sum Raw (Fin hiddenCount))
  let Hidden := PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin hiddenCount)
  let enc := fun F : Finset Cl => ∀ x : Raw → Bool,
    (∃ j : Fin m, ∀ i : Fin n, x (j,i) = true) ↔
      ∃ z : Fin hiddenCount → Bool, PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Satisfies (Sum.elim x z) (↑F : Set _)
  let consistent := fun U : Finset Hidden =>
    ∃ z : Fin hiddenCount → Bool, PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Satisfies z (↑U : Set _)
  (∃ F : Finset Cl, enc F ∧ (∀ C ∈ F, C.card ≤ W) ∧
    (∑ C ∈ F, price C.card) ≤ K) ↔
  ∃ (U : Finset Hidden) (g : Hidden → ℕ),
    ¬ consistent U ∧ (∀ H ∈ U, consistent (U.erase H)) ∧
    (∑ H ∈ U, g H) = m ∧ (∀ H ∈ U, H.card + g H ≤ W) ∧
    (∑ H ∈ U, n^(g H) * price (H.card + g H)) ≤ K
changed.unlocks: Transforms a total-width encoding problem into a finite optimization over minimally unsatisfiable clauses on its hidden variables.
changed.context: Miss one uniform input in each block. Project the surviving false-input clauses to hidden bits and choose a minimal unsatisfiable subformula, with one original clause per member. Every missing input repairs the table and must occur positively in a chosen clause. Assign blocks to these clauses. A clause with u positive inputs survives with probability at most n^(-u), so averaging pays for the assigned groups. Conversely expand each hidden clause by all choices of one input per assigned block.

Conversely expand each hidden clause by all choices of one input per assigned block.

changed.title: One-a-side promise: the 4 by 5 bipartite graph with mask 101884 has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit of at most 9 gates
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun (u : Fin 4) (v : Fin 5) => (101884 : ℕ).testBit (5 * u.val + v.val)) 9
changed.unlocks: the AND/OR cost of 4 by 5 graphs off the square, where the checked twin merge sends square graphs, for the silent-line work
changed.sketch: A search unit. We hold a circuit of 10 AND/OR gates (three plain forms, full lines taken out and equal gates merged); at this size those forms are weak; we hold none of 9; this is a search. Our count of unread rows and columns gives a floor of 8 (on paper), a gap of 2. Answer with a gate list (AND or OR, each reading at most two wires; wires 0 to 3 left, 4 to 8 right, gate j writes wire 9 + j, each gate reading only earlier wires) and its output wire, judged on all 20 inputs with one vertex on each side.
